children.translated_text: <s>Caturvargasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of the Four Goals).

body.translated_text: Composed by the great poet, the illustrious <s>Kṣemendra</s>.

children.translated_text: First chapter.
shaded by patience, adorned with the vine of auspicious thought, rooted in moral conduct,
The trunk of <s>Dharma</s>, sprinkled with the pure nectar of youthful compassion,
may <s>Dharma</s> bear the fruit of prosperity for the blessed! //
with leaves shimmering as the blossoming of beings, with flowers of bursting merit —
For the instruction of students and the satisfaction of the wise,
<s>Kṣemendra</s> composes this <s>Vargasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of Goals) in his own verses. //

children.text: dharmaḥ śarma paratra ceha ca nṛṇāṃ dharmo 'ndhakāre raviḥ

children.translated_text: capable of pacifying all calamities, the treasure known as <s>Dharma</s> belongs to the noble-minded.
<s>Dharma</s> is happiness for men in the next world and in this; <s>Dharma</s> is the sun in darkness;

children.text: dharmo bandhur abāndhave pṛthupathe dharmaḥ suhṛn niścalaḥ
saṃsārorumarusthale suratarur nāsty eva dharmāt paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A wish-fulfilling tree in the great desert of <s>saṃsāra</s> — there is nothing superior to <s>Dharma</s>. //
<s>Dharma</s> is a kinsman when one has no kinsmen; on the broad road, <s>Dharma</s> is a steadfast friend.

children.text: karṇe dharmakathā mukhe paricitaṃ dharmābhirāmaṃ vacaś

children.translated_text: in the mind, the aspiration of <s>Dharma</s>; everywhere, a devoted establishment in <s>Dharma</s>;
In the ear, the discourse on <s>Dharma</s>; in the mouth, speech well-versed in the delight of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: kāye dharmamayī kriyā parikaraḥ so 'yaṃ śubhaprāptaye

children.translated_text: whose fruit remains untouched by the waves of calamity even at the end of a cosmic age. //
in the body, action made of <s>Dharma</s> — this is the equipment for attaining the good,

children.text: buddhyā hīno manuṣyaḥ śubhaphalavikalas tulyaceṣṭaḥ paśūnām |
children.translated_text: a human devoid of intellect, lacking the fruit of goodness, acts no differently from animals.
Blameworthy is that birth, shrouded in the most enduring darkness of delusion, which lacks humanity;
learning devoid of <s>Dharma</s> is merely the fruitless toil of parrot-like speech. //
Intellect devoid of learning wanders in the examination and investigation of the true nature of real and unreal;
The learning of those blinded by pride, which destroys the excellence of others —
that is merely an elephant's bath, [washed away] by the dust of envy. //

children.text: tatprājñatvaṃ harati vimalaṃ yena śīlaṃ na kāmas

children.translated_text: that is true steadfastness by which the sense-faculties are brought under the power of tranquility.
That is true wisdom by which moral conduct, not desire, carries one away spotlessly;
that is true learning by which the disgrace of existence attains peace. //
That is true cleverness by which the world-conquering illusion (<s>māyā</s>) is deceived;

children.text: andhaḥ sa eva śrutavarjito yaḥ śaṭhaḥ sa evārthinirarthako yaḥ |
children.translated_text: Blind indeed is he who is devoid of learning; deceitful is he who is useless to those in need;

children.text: mṛtaḥ sa evāsti yaśo na yasya dharme na dhīr yasya sa eva śocyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dead is he who has no fame — he who has no resolve regarding <s>Dharma</s> is truly pitiable. //

children.text: hitaṃ na kiṃcid vihitaṃ parasya dattaṃ na vittaṃ na ca satyam uktam |
children.translated_text: No benefit has been rendered to another; no wealth has been given; no truth has been spoken —

children.text: yasmin dine niṣphalatāṃ prayātam āyuḥ sa kālaḥ paridevanasya ||
children.translated_text: on whatever day one's life has passed in fruitlessness, that time is for lamentation. //

children.text: na dānatulyaṃ dhanam anyad asti na satyatulyaṃ vratam anyad asti |
children.translated_text: There is no wealth equal to generosity; there is no vow equal to truthfulness;

children.text: na śītatulyaṃ śubham anyad asti na kṣāntitulyaṃ hitam anyad asti ||
children.translated_text: there is no auspiciousness equal to tranquility; there is no benefit equal to patience. //
the release of generosity from the hand, thought concerned with the end of the affliction of self-generation in the mind,
Truthfulness in speech, the practice of serenity in one's gaze, reassuring all intentions,

children.text: saṃsaktā hṛdaye dayaiva dayitā kāye parārthodyamo
yasyaikaḥ puruṣaḥ sa jīvati bhave bhrāmyanty ajīvāḥ pare ||
children.translated_text: that one person truly lives in this existence; all others wander about, lifeless. //
compassion alone as the beloved clinging to the heart, exertion for the benefit of others in the body —
compassion alone in this world is the nectar of life for all people.
Compassion alone, whose thoughts are devoted to the protection of others' lives, is the mother of <s>Dharma</s>;
in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the praiseworthy path of one's own city of virtue. //
Non-violence, declared by the sages with the eyes of knowledge, is an uncommon merit —

children.text: prāṇāṇāṃ parirakṣaṇāya satataṃ sarvāḥ kriyāḥ prāṇiṇāṃ
prāṇebhyo 'py adhikaṃ samastajagatāṃ nasty eva kiṃcit priyam |
children.translated_text: for all the worlds, there is nothing dearer than life itself.
All activities of living beings are for the protection of life at all times;

children.text: puṇyaṃ tasya na śakyate gaṇayituṃ yaḥ pūrṇakāruṇyavān
prāṇānām abhayaṃ dadāti sukṛtī teṣām ahiṃsāvrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that meritorious one who gives fearlessness to living beings, whose vow is non-violence. //
The merit of one who is full of compassion cannot be counted —
He alone is the ground for the splendor of the ornament of beings, the ornament of the upper and lower worlds, the supreme among men,

children.text: mukhāmbuje yasya vasaty anatyayā sadaiva satyābharaṇā sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: in whose lotus-mouth dwells forever the unfailing <s>Sarasvatī</s>, adorned with truth. //

children.text: vittaṃ kleśānimittam eva malinaṃ yātu svayaṃ tatkṣayam |
children.translated_text: wealth that is impure, the very cause of affliction — let it go to ruin on its own!
Wealth that is moist [from hoarding], sitting in the treasury, fruitless to supplicants, a thorn to others,

children.text: svārthāsaktam anarthasārthasadanaṃ mā māstu tat kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: attached to its own interests, a dwelling for the caravan of misfortune — may it not belong to anyone! //
A body devoid of compassion and service to others, a mere burden on the earth,
Worshipful among men, even worshipped by the gods, through acts of accumulating the merit of compassion —
one whose body is adorned with service to others attains the essence of <s>saṃsāra</s>. //
affectionate toward another's love, patient with endurance for another's insults,
Free from desire for another's property, without curiosity about another's wife,
striving to remove others' suffering — such a person exists through abundant merit. //
skilled in praising others, free from disparaging others' virtues,

children.text: padmānām iva sā satāṃ saguṇatā yā saṃśrayārhā śriyaḥ
sā śrīr bhadragajendramūrtir iva yā dānena vibhrājate |
children.translated_text: that prosperity which shines through generosity is like the noble form of a great lordly elephant.
That virtue of the good which is worthy of being the refuge of prosperity is like that of lotuses;

children.text: tad dānaṃ navacandravad yad aniśaṃ mānena saṃpūryate
māno 'sau ṭṛṇavan na yaḥ paricayamlānaḥ śanaiḥ śuṣyati ||
children.translated_text: that honor which is like grass — not wilting with familiarity, not gradually drying up. //
That generosity which is constantly filled with honor is like a new moon;

children.text: lakṣmīr dānaphalā śrutaṃ śamaphalaṃ pāṇiḥ surārcāphalaś

children.translated_text: action has its fruit in <s>Dharma</s>; life has its fruit in the play of removing others' suffering.
Wealth has its fruit in generosity; learning has its fruit in tranquility; the hand has its fruit in worship of the gods;

children.text: bhavyānāṃ bhavaśānticintanaphalā bhūtyai bhavaty eva dhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the virtuous, the intellect, whose fruit is the contemplation of the pacification of existence, conduces to prosperity indeed. //
Speech has its fruit in truthfulness; eminence, abundant, has its fruit in the happiness of the world;

children.text: śīlaṃ śilayatāṃ kulaṃ kalayatāṃ sadbhāvam abhyasyatāṃ
vyājaṃ varjayatāṃ guṇaṃ gaṇayatāṃ dharme dhiyaṃ badhnatām |
children.translated_text: Abandon deceit! Treasure virtue! Fix your mind on <s>Dharma</s>!
Cultivate moral conduct! Foster your family! Practice good faith!

children.text: kṣāntiṃ cintayatāṃ tamaḥ śamayatāṃ tattvaśrutiṃ śṛṇvatāṃ
saṃsāre na paropakārasadṛśaṃ paśyāmi puṇyaṃ satām ||
children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s>, I see no merit of the good equal to service to others. //
Contemplate patience! Extinguish darkness! Listen to the discourse on truth!
Pilgrimages with the exertion of long journeys; rituals with great expenditure and extravagant display;

children.text: tapāṃsi muktvā tanuśoṣaṇāni hiṃsāvirāme ramatāṃ matir vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: austerities that emaciate the body — abandoning all these, may your mind delight in the cessation of violence! //

children.text: yujvā vipraḥ śucir anucaraḥ saṃyatātmā tapasvī

children.translated_text: a learned counselor, a king who is the ornament of the earth's ladies —
A devoted priest, a pure attendant, a self-controlled ascetic,
this is the complete sowing of the seed of the future tree of the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age). //
when in the garden of <s>Dharma</s>, being sprinkled with the torrential waters of good deeds,

children.text: dambhena śīlavratam aspṛhatvaṃ viraktatā śrotriyatā mṛdutvam |
children.translated_text: Hypocrisy as moral observance and vows; covetousness as renunciation;
learning as gentleness — these are the roots of the tree of the <s>Kali</s> (Dark Age), hiding deep, crooked crookedness. //

children.text: yāvanti dānāni vadanti santas tapāṃsi tīrthāni ca yāni santi |
children.translated_text: Whatever acts of generosity the good teach, whatever austerities and pilgrimages exist —

children.text: tatpuṇyam ekatra vibhāti sarvaṃ mahārham ekatra ca niḥspṛhatvam ||
children.translated_text: all that merit shines forth in one place, and desirelessness shines forth supremely in one place. //
Freedom from wretchedness is the beauty of the face of the good; freedom from greed is the inner voice of non-solicitation;

children.text: kāyasya satsevyam asevyakatvaṃ pāṇer anuttānatalatvam eva ||
children.translated_text: not resorting to what should not be resorted to is the [adornment] of the body; the hand's [adornment] is simply its palm not being extended [in begging]. //

children.text: mānyaḥ kulīnaḥ kulajāt kalāvān vidvān kalājñād viduṣaḥ suśīlaḥ |
children.translated_text: One of good family is honored more than a well-born person; a learned one more than one skilled in arts; one of good conduct more than a scholar;

children.text: dhanī suśīlād dhanino 'pi dātā dātur jitā kīrtir āyācakena ||
children.translated_text: a wealthy one more than one of good conduct; a generous one more than a wealthy one; and the fame of a generous one is conquered by a non-beggar. //

children.text: taptais tīvravrataiḥ kiṃ vikasati karuṇāsyandinī yady ahiṃsā
kiṃ dūrais tīrthasārair yadi śamavimalaṃ mānasaṃ satyapūtam |
children.translated_text: What is the use of distant pilgrimages, if the mind is pure with tranquility and purified by truth?
What is the use of severe austerities, if non-violence overflowing with compassion blossoms?

children.text: yatnād anyopakāre prasarati yadi dhīr dānapuṇyaiḥ kim anyaiḥ
kiṃ mokṣopāyayogair yadi śucimanasām ucyate bhaktir asti ||
children.translated_text: What need of practices for liberation, if it is said that devotion exists for those of pure mind? //
If the intellect extends to helping others with effort, what need of other meritorious acts of generosity?
Thus ends the first chapter, called 'Praise of <s>Dharma</s>.'
Second chapter.

children.text: pradhānadhāmnāṃ nidhaye dhanāya namo' stu tasmai guṇino 'pi yatnāt |
children.translated_text: Salutation to that wealth (<s>dhana</s>), the abode of the foremost glories, by which even virtuous men's effort

children.text: yadāśayā nirguṇabhūpatīnām agre guṇān ṣaṇyadaśāṃ nayanti ||
children.translated_text: and intention cause the virtues of kings devoid of merit to attain the state of sixfold multiplied [glory]. //

children.text: dānādidharmaḥ kriyate dhanena dhanena dhanyā dhanam āpnuvanti |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> beginning with generosity is performed through wealth; the wealthy obtain wealth through their blessedness.

children.text: dhanair vinā kāmakathāpi nāsti trivargamūlaṃ dhanam eva nānyat ||
children.translated_text: Without wealth, there is not even talk of desire; wealth alone, nothing else, is the root of the three goals of life (<s>trivarga</s>). //
that which fools chew on for a long time — the parrot-like prattle of poets in comfortable ease,
That which cowards direct as ferocious play of cock-fighting like warriors,

children.text: nīcair uccataraś ca sevakahayaḥ svāmyena yad vāhyate

children.translated_text: that is the haughty, arrogant display, the dwelling place of the dance of wealth's caprice. //
that which causes the low to ride a servant's horse as if they were masters, higher [than they are] —

children.text: pūjā dhanenaiva na satkulena kīrtir dhanenaiva na vikrameṇa |
children.translated_text: Worship comes through wealth alone, not through good family; fame through wealth alone, not through valor;

children.text: rūpaṃ dhanenaiva na yauvanena kriyā dhanenaiva na jīvitena ||
children.translated_text: beauty through wealth alone, not through youth; action through wealth alone, not through mere living. //

children.text: vṛddhāḥ prasiddhā vibudhā vidagdhāḥ śūrā śrutijñāḥ kavayaḥ kulīnāḥ |
children.translated_text: Elders, the renowned, the learned, the clever, heroes, knowers of scripture, poets, the well-born —

children.text: vilokayantaḥ sadhanasya vaktraṃ jayeti jīveti sadā vadanti ||
children.translated_text: gazing upon the face of a wealthy man, they always say 'Victory!' and 'Long life!' //

children.text: kruddhyā yutaṃ niścalapakṣmanetraṃ maunānvitaṃ devam ivākulīnam |
children.translated_text: With unblinking, steadfast eyes joined with anger, as if divine yet silent and unperturbed,

children.text: dīnaḥ kulīnaḥ praṇamatkulīnaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ stauti dhanābhikāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the well-born but poor man bows to the base-born rich man with folded hands and praises him, desiring wealth. //

children.text: tasmād alabdhadraviṇasya lābhe labdhasya rakṣāniyame yatena |
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should exert effort in acquiring wealth not [yet] acquired,

children.text: saṃrakṣamāṇasya sadā vivṛddhau vṛddhasya ca sthānavibhāgasarge ||
children.translated_text: in guarding and regulating what has been acquired, in always increasing what is being guarded, and in properly allocating and distributing what has increased. //
[serves] the acquisition of position, energy, increase, victory, life, learning, and arts,
When it supports <s>Dharma</s>, is regulated as purely as the moon, [serves] wife, friends, and kinsmen,
in the relinquishing of wealth — the good feel no knotted attachment or bondage. //
at the praiseworthy time of the body's repose, in an undisputed distribution,
Gatherings with rogues, the round of wandering entertainers, delight in courtesans, the scent of special ascetics,

children.text: spardhā suveṣair nijavṛttilajjā pradhānam etan nidhanaṃ dhanānām ||
children.translated_text: rivalry with the well-dressed, shame regarding one's own livelihood — this is the chief cause of the destruction of wealth. //

children.text: duṣpūro gurur arthabhoganicayair bandhur daridraḥ śaṭhaḥ |
children.translated_text: a teacher insatiable by heaps of wealth and enjoyment; a kinsman who is poor and treacherous;
A wife devoid of virtue, a spendthrift; a friend whose body is full of deceit;

children.text: dāsaś cauryaparo 'salaś ca kupade putraḥ khalaiḥ pātitaḥ

children.translated_text: this is the visible ruin of the treasury accumulated through hundreds of afflictions.
a servant given to theft and unsteady in a bad situation; a son brought down by wicked men —
boldness rains jewels; self-restraint is the uprooting of the forest of misfortune;
Skill is the root of wealth; acquaintance with good policy is the watering of prosperity's garden;
laziness is the frost unbearable to the lotus of people's wealth.
the guarding of counsel is the protection of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune); avoiding wicked people is the quelling of calamity;
Inability to endure cold, fear of the sun's heat, preoccupation with gossip, waiting for companions on the road,

children.text: lajjābhimānaḥ kṣaṇasaṃmukhatvaṃ nakṣatracarcā ca dhanasya vighnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: bashfulness and pride, attending only to the moment, and astrologizing — these are obstacles to wealth.
Concern with dress and particular hardships, obstructing others, arrogance from being one's own master —

children.text: nadīphalānām iva śīghragānāṃ hānir dhanānāṃ grahaṇe vilambaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like river fruits that swiftly pass away, delay in seizing wealth is the loss of riches.
By heavy-charging astrologers [the wealth] of the foolish; by thieves and rats skilled in diminishing, [the wealth] of merchants;
by hordes of scribes and bards — the fortune of kings is consumed.

children.text: dāridryeṇa kulaṃ madena kuśalaṃ dveṣeṇa vidyāphalaṃ

children.translated_text: by association with the wicked, virtue; by impure conduct, bright fame;
By poverty, family [honor]; by intoxication, merit; by hatred, the fruit of learning;

children.text: ālasyena dhanaṃ prayāti nidhanaṃ laulyena mānonnatir

children.translated_text: and by the acceptance of the wretchedness of begging, the entire cluster of a person's good qualities [perishes].
by laziness, wealth goes to ruin; by fickleness, the elevation of honor;

children.text: maugdhyān mṛgarthī raghunandano 'pi bāṇaḥ pramādād balir ārjavena |
children.translated_text: Even <s>Rāma</s>, the joy of the <s>Raghus</s>, through naiveté [in chasing] the deer; <s>Bāṇa</s> through carelessness; <s>Bali</s> through honesty;

children.text: nalaḥ kusaṅgena yayātijaś ca kleśāsahatvād vyasanāny avāpuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nala</s> through bad company; and the son of <s>Yayāti</s> through inability to endure affliction — all obtained calamities.
Naiveté, carelessness, distrust, bad company, and fear of hardship —

children.text: pañca saṃkocadā doṣāḥ padminyā iva saṃpadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these five are faults that cause prosperity to close up, as [cold causes] a lotus to close.
Through the sense faculties — named as openings in vessels resembling pots —
the wealth obtained by clinging to the depths of bad wells and pits flows out like water.

children.text: dīpe rūparatāḥ prayānti satatāpātāt pataṅgāḥ kṣayam |
children.translated_text: moths, delighting in form, perish from the constant falling [into] a lamp;
In the sweet, freshly fragrant heart of the lotus, bees find imprisonment;

children.text: gītenaiva mṛgāḥ patanti kariṇīsparśena nītā gajās
tasmād indriyasaktir eva sahasā puṃsāṃ vipaddūtikā ||
children.translated_text: therefore, attachment to the senses is indeed the sudden harbinger of calamity for men.
deer fall [captive] by song alone; elephants are led away by the touch of a female elephant —

children.text: kulaṃ kuvṛttyā kaluṣīkṛtaṃ taiḥ kṛto guṇaughas tṛnatulyamūlyaḥ |
children.translated_text: By those who did not acquire and preserve wealth, family honor is polluted by bad conduct,

children.text: mānasya mūle nihitaḥ kuṭhāraḥ prāptaṃ na vittaṃ parirakṣitaṃ yaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the flood of virtues is rendered worth no more than straw, and an axe is placed at the root of honor.

children.text: jātaḥ satkulajaḥ sa nīcavinayī sevāvamānair adhas

children.translated_text: has fallen grievously beneath [his station], and the fire of curse blazes against his own honor and fame;
He who is born of a good family yet serves the low with servile humility,

children.text: vittaṃ yena na rakṣitaṃ ripumukhaṃ tena sthitaṃ vīkṣitam ||
children.translated_text: he who did not protect his wealth has been left staring into the face of his enemy.
he, being ill-fortuned, has swallowed the poison of begging placed by his own hand;

children.text: dhāvan sevitum eti sādhur adhamaṃ kandhyas tato yāty asau
nītā mūlyatulāṃ guṇāś ca guṇibhiḥ kaścin na gṛhṇāti tān |
children.translated_text: virtues, weighed on the scale of price by the virtuous — no one takes them;
Running to serve, the good man goes to a base person, and is then turned back from the threshold;

children.text: yācñā mānamahāśanir dhanakṛtā prāptaṃ na kiṃcit tayā
kiṃ kiṃ vā na vidhīyate dhanadhiyā dhanyaḥ sa yasyāsti tat ||
children.translated_text: what indeed is not done by the thought of wealth? Blessed is he who possesses it.
begging, the great thunderbolt against honor, is caused by [lack of] wealth, yet nothing is obtained by it —
the labor of wandering through continents, roads, and mountains in [all] directions,
Acquaintance with learning and arts, service of kings,
'that is obtainable by wealth' — so runs the maxim of the wealthy.
and acts of war in this world — all are from greed for the gain of food;

children.text: yāvat tṛptisukhodayena na janaḥ kṣutkṣāmakukṣiḥ kṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: so long do discourses on <s>Dharma</s>, delight in love, and desire for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) arise;
As long as a person's belly is not for a moment emaciated with the torments of hunger,

children.text: prāpte bhojanacintanasya samaye vittaṃ nimittaṃ vinā
dharme kasya dhiyaḥ smaraṃ smarati kaḥ kenekṣyate mokṣabhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: who has thought for <s>Dharma</s>? Who remembers <s>Smara</s> (love)? By whom is the realm of <s>mokṣa</s> contemplated?
but when the time for thinking about food arrives, without wealth as the means,
intolerant of others, shameless in reciting praises of his own false virtues;
The hypocrite, skilled in harsh wandering [for alms], knows how to attract wealth from the dull-witted rich,

children.text: āryaḥ kuryān na sevaṃ kulavinayaguṇais tena mūko 'rthanāyāṃ
tīkṣṇānāṃ mārgaṇānāṃ bhavati hi purataḥ kṣmāpater lakṣalābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for before the king, it is the sharp petitioners who obtain a hundred thousand.
a noble man would not perform such service, hence through family, discipline, and virtue he is mute in the pursuit of wealth —
Thus ends the second chapter, named 'The Praise of Wealth.'
Third Chapter.
as if painted with clusters of fluttering [glances] having the luster of blue lotus gardens,
With rolling eyes playfully rising from the charming sport of graceful women,

children.text: kusumadhanuṣaḥ śyāmā mūrtis tanotu sukhāni vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may the dark form of the bearer of the flower-bow (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) bestow happiness upon you!
and as if covered by rows of bees, her fragrant companions, with clipped wings —
like [garlands] with chief gems of blue sapphire, with pearl-strands released,
Radiant like the unfolding of a single petal of the <s>ketakī</s> flower with wandering bees,
triumph — those flashes of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) and <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) from the eyes of deer-eyed women!
the eyes [of lovely women], like crescents of the moon marked with tiny spots of eyelashes,

children.text: kratuṃ dhanānāṃ phalam agryam āhuḥ phalaṃ kratūnām avivādi puṇyam |
children.translated_text: They say sacrifice is the highest fruit of wealth; the fruit of sacrifice is undisputed merit;

children.text: puṇyasya pūrṇaṃ phalam indraloko dviraṣṭvarṣāḥ striya eva nākaḥ ||
